Following the shutdown of TV Time last month, co-founder Antonio Pinto has announced the launch of Bingers, a brand-new TV and movie tracking app with a stronger emphasis on social features. Here are the details.

Bingers is now available for download

Whip Media had earlier announced it would shut down the TV tracking app TV Time, and one of the app's co-founders promptly announced the launch of Bingers, describing it as "a fast and stylish watchlist that's also a fun community".

Now, according to TechCrunch, Bingers is already available for download on iOS and Android, offering users who have yet to find a replacement a spiritual successor — TV Time itself was once one of the most widely used TV tracking apps in the world.

Former TV Time users who used the platform's export tool before it was shut down to save their data can import their files into Bingers and pick up where they left off; users who didn't export their data, or new users who have never used a TV tracking app, can start from scratch.

Bingers places heavy emphasis on community-driven features, such as user profiles, comments, episode ratings, GIFs, polls, and character voting. Pinto told TechCrunch that these features were precisely the key to TV Time's long-term appeal:

For users who simply want a platform to keep track of TV shows and movies they've watched, Bingers offers dedicated watchlists and viewing history. Like TV Time, it also displays a calendar of upcoming episodes and premiere dates, along with a countdown showing how many days until the premiere.

Bingers is available for free on the App Store and currently has no in-app purchases.
